chunks: It is a promise of God; and God does not go back on His promise. Yet most men do not understand:
ai.seo_question: What does it mean that God does not break His promise?
ai.summary: In the context of the Roman-Byzantine victory over the Persians, this verse reassures the early Muslims that the divine promise of victory (as foretold in the preceding verses) is absolute, contrasting with the general human ignorance of divine timing. Shia scholars often highlight this as a testament to God's fidelity (al-Wa'd al-Haqq) and use it to illustrate how the masses (al-Akthar) remain unaware of the deeper realities of divine decree despite clear signs.
